text:
maya: FYI ACME reported a huge p99 jump on Dedicated this morning around 03:20 UTC. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~4x. Only affects their reserved pool acme-prod. No API errors in logs, just long attach/warmup times and backlog in scaleup queue.

aj: copying metrics — can you paste the pool id + a few request ids? also any recent config or image changes to that pool?

maya: pool: acme-prod (pool-az1-red). sample req ids: r_9f3a, r_9f3b, r_9f3c. No config changes on their side; they hit it during a billing-window burst.

olga: seeing same in infra dash — attach p99 ~18s (baseline ~1.2s). queue depth spiked to 120 for ~7m. New kernel-image push at 02:58 might be correlated (large image + slower pulls).

aj: that could explain cold GPU attach slowness. If image pull is >10s, attach handoff queues up and autoscaler keeps waiting. Any image-pull errors in node logs?

liam: deploy-bot posted the image rollout: kernel-image:v5.3.2 -> pushed 02:55 UTC to eu-west-1 pool nodes. SHA increased image size by ~700MB.

olga: node logs show repeated docker pull timeouts during the spike window: "error pulling image: context deadline exceeded" then backoff. warmup scripts retry a few times — increases attachment delay.

aj: okay. immediate mitigations: 1) pause rollout to acme-prod nodes 2) manually prewarm X GPUs in that pool 3) temporarily route gold-tier traffic to hosted fallback for ACME 4) lower autoscale attach timeout to fail fast and trigger fallback. which can we do quickly?

maya: I can enable hosted fallback routing for their API key (ACME) now. Doing that.

liam: pausing rollout done. rolling back kernel-image on acme-prod nodes to v5.3.1 — applying now.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for pool-az1-red at 03:38 UTC.

olga: manual prewarm: starting 4 GPUs in acme-prod as a hotpool (prewarm command run). expect them ready in ~45s.

aj: also suggest short-term config tweak: increase min_pool for acme-prod by +2 and set min_pool_timeout to 5m so autoscaler keeps a small buffer during billing windows. I'll prepare a patch.

maya: hosted fallback active — ~60% of ACME traffic now routed to hosted nodes, their app latency improved immediately. ticket updated.

aj: quick root-cause hypothesis: larger image rollout increased image-pull times -> node attach timeouts -> long scale-up queues -> p95/p99 spike. Mitigations: rollback image, prewarm, route to hosted, and add guardrail in platform: reject image pushes >200MB delta without canary subset and pull-time benchmarking.

liam: agree. I'll open a platform task to add a pre-deploy image-size check and cluster pull-time smoke test. Also propose prioritizing warmup images (smaller base) for reserved pools.

olga: monitoring note: we've turned on attach-time alarms (p99 > 3s) for all Dedicated pools and an automated prewarm trigger at 80% queue depth.

aj: actions assigned: liam will add pre-deploy checks (ETA EOD), olga will keep attach alarms and automated prewarm enabled, I will push the min_pool patch for acme-prod (temporary), maya will keep customer updated.

maya: customer updated — they see p99 back to near baseline. will keep monitoring for 30m. Thanks team :heart:

sre-bot: incident-summary: acme-prod p99 regression (03:20-03:44 UTC) root cause suspected: large kernel-image push causing image-pull timeouts -> attach lag -> queue buildup. mitigations applied: rollback, prewarm, hosted fallback, autoscale guards.

maya: closing loop — will open a postmortem doc with timelines and customer impact once we have logs consolidated.

aj: quick note for follow-up: add test to CI that simulates image-pull slowdowns and measures attach latency for our autoscaler. low-effort but high impact.

maya: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
